For some bound HVSs (see Brown et al. 2007), and also HVS HE 0437-5439 (Edelmann et al. 2005) there exists a discrepancy between their kinematics and apparent ages.
Since the star likely originated from the GC (Brown et al. 2010), it is quite possible that this HVS is a rejuvenated star, originally ejected as a binary from the GC (see Perets I).

notes: HE 0437-5439: the paper treats this as a known HVS, discussing its kinematics/age discrepancy and a possible rejuvenated-binary origin (T:p5-b1, T:p6-b11). It is therefore follow-up rather than a newly selected candidate; T:p5-b1 refers to "some bound HVSs" separately, while the paper's defined HVS criterion at T:p1-b9 is sufficient speed to escape the Galaxy. No other individually identified star is supported as a Galactic unbound candidate; generic HVS/HVB/S-star references lack individual names.

HE 0437-5439: The target star HE 0437-5439 is mentioned only incidentally in this theoretical paper on triple disruptions by a massive black hole. Text at T:p5-b1 refers to "HVS HE 0437-5439 (Edelmann et al. 2005)" in the context of a kinematics/age discrepancy, and text at T:p6-b11 notes it "has been identified as a true young B2 III-IV halo star with mass ~9 M⊙ (Bonanos et al. 2008; Przybilla et al. 2008)". Neither passage reports any of the quantities listed (right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probabilities). The reported stellar mass is not an identifier among the requested quantities, so no values are extracted.
